result.title: Jev-DLC: Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback
result.summary: Individual preferences often become visible only after deployment, when a user accepts one decision or revokes it in favor of another. Jev-style typed interfaces make this feedback explicit by identifying the selected action and, under revocation, the decision it replaces. We study how these consequences persist across requests as Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback (Jev-DLC). Jev-DLC treats each correction as both evidence about a recurring action identity and a directed relation between the preferred and rejected choices. It preserves these signals in complementary bounded channels above a frozen scorer and combines their scores to shape the next decision. The method retains no raw interaction history, adds no scorer call, and performs no runtime language-model backward pass. We also introduce TCPA-Bench, a chronological suite that credits a correction only through its effect on later decisions. On TCPA-Repeat, Jev-DLC reaches 44.83% user-macro accuracy overall, 2.43 points above Recent-4 history replay. After at least two earlier feedback events, it reaches 56.07%, a 7.54-point margin over the strongest reported comparison at this depth. These results show how explicit typed corrections can become compact causal state for continual personalization.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究如何从显式类型化反馈（用户接受某动作，或撤销并指明被替换的决策）进行决策级持续学习：把每次纠正视为动作身份的偏好证据与偏好—被拒选项之间的有向关系，保存在冻结评分器之上的互补有界通道中并融合打分，另构建只按对后续决策的实际影响计分的时序基准 TCPA-Bench。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「冻结主干＋有界外部状态增量更新」与「仅以后续决策效果归因反馈」的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的更新方式与监督信号贡献分配、因果式评价提供可核查线索，但该文不含视觉或多模态推理内容。
